plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful ornamental tree covered in clouds of delicate, fragrant blossoms that appear before the leaves. It is celebrated worldwide and is the centerpiece of hanami flower-viewing festivals.
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The 3,000 cherry trees gifted by Tokyo to Washington D.C. in 1912 are the origin of the National Cherry Blossom Festival.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A spring bulb with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems, available in countless cultivars. Mass plantings create vivid carpets of color in gardens and fields.
plants.location: Netherlands, Northern Europe, North America, and cultivated temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: During 'Tulip Mania' in the 1630s Netherlands, single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree native to eastern North America whose clusters of magenta-pink flowers burst directly from bare branches and even the trunk, followed by heart-shaped leaves.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, northern Mexico
plants.funFact: The flowers are edible and are sometimes used in salads; the trunk-flowering habit is called cauliflory.

plants.name: Nemophila menziesii
plants.description: A low-growing annual wildflower with delicate, saucer-shaped sky-blue flowers with white centers. It carpets grasslands and hillsides in wet spring seasons.
plants.location: California and Oregon, USA; naturalized in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: In Japan's Hitachi Seaside Park, millions of Nemophila bloom in mid-April, turning entire hills into a sea of blue.
